REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1, u2, u3, u4
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u4
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, blocker_moved & !has_door_key) -> u1
(u0, has_door_key) -> u2
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, has_door_key & blocker_moved) -> u2
(u1, has_door_key & !blocker_moved) -> u2
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, door_open) -> u3
(u2, key_lost) -> u2
(u2, else) -> u2
(u3, target_picked_up) -> u4
(u3, else) -> u3
(u4, else) -> u4
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, blocker_moved & !has_door_key, u1) -> 0.1
(u1, has_door_key & blocker_moved, u2) -> 0.1
(u2, door_open, u3) -> 0.2
(u2, key_lost, u2) -> -0.1
(u3, target_picked_up, u4) -> 1.0
feedback: Accepted. Format: the artifact matches the paper's structure exactly (REWARD_MACHINE header, STATES, INITIAL_STATE, FINAL_STATES, TRANSITION_FUNCTION, REWARD_FUNCTION); FINAL_STATES is nonempty, u4 is declared in STATES, and it is the accepting state reached precisely on target_picked_up, the event that terminates the episode. Propositions: only the five environment propositions appear (no invented has_ball/carrying, consistent with the code notes), and labels are predicate-only (& / ! / else). Totality and reachability: every state has a per-state else self-loop absorbing irrelevant events (idle steps, ball handling, key re-pickups, door re-shutting), all five states are reachable, and u4 is reachable on every feasible order, including the key-first order the environment highlights (u0→u2 on has_door_key; the forced drop fires key_lost in u2 with -0.1; the ball move and key re-pick stay in u2 via else; then door_open→u3→u4). Persistent/event distinction is respected: key_lost is used as a one-step penalty self-loop rather than a state feature, conditions serve as guards, and u2 latches through key re-pickups so 'open it later' is supported. Ordered coverage is complete and non-deadlocking: (u1, has_door_key & blocker_moved) rewards the compliant key take, while (u1, has_door_key & !blocker_moved)→u2 (implicitly 0, consistent with the implicit-zero convention used for the else loops) usefully routes the ball-put-back case into u2 so its forced drop is penalized there — without that line, key_lost would land in u1 unpenalized. Reward safety: progress rewards are dense across the four milestones (0.1, 0.1, 0.2, terminal 1.0) and bounded; each positive transition is one-way and fires at most once, so no positive reward farming; the only repeatable transition (u2, key_lost, u2) is negative and bounded, a pure deterrent for dropping the key while the door is closed. The constraint 'take the key only after the ball is out of the way' is enforced incentive-wise: an early key take forfeits both 0.1 shaping terms and its mandatory drop costs -0.1 (net about -0.3 versus the compliant order, which remains strictly best). Regressions are correctly not required here: door_open latches in u3 (re-opening is unrewarded and physics forces re-opening before the box), and ball-return is handled by latching u1 plus the blocker_moved re-check inside the u1→u2 reward guard, which avoids 0.1 farming from pick-up/drop-back cycles. Minor note: key_lost after the door has been opened and re-shut (u3) is absorbed by the else self-loop without penalty, which is acceptable since 'still closed' no longer applies once the door has been open and the key is no longer needed.

feedback: All five declared propositions are implemented with no extras, no imports, no actions, and no mutations of env or episode_memory. blocker_moved scans for the door cell and checks the cell at (x-1, y): this matches the documented geometry (ball starts at (dx-1, dy), start room on the left), is true when the ball is carried or dropped elsewhere, and false again when dropped back on that cell. Grid.get(-1, y) safely returns None at x=0, so the left-neighbor read is runtime-safe. has_door_key, door_open, and target_picked_up match the documented expressions exactly (carrying type/color checks, door color match, is_open scan, mission string f-string). key_lost is a correct event: previous_valuation['has_door_key'] AND NOT has_door_key (inlined identically to the standalone function) AND NOT door_open (inlined identically), evaluated against the read-only previous valuation; the extra truthiness guard on previous_valuation and the redundant double negation are harmless no-ops that preserve boolean fidelity and cannot fire at the first step. Syntax is valid; only documented API is used (grid.get, carrying, mission, width, height, object type/color/is_open, episode_memory read).
